data.reasoning: Both models agree the PKGBUILD and .SRCINFO are safe. The package is a straightforward binary package that downloads a 7z archive from the project's own website (septabee.nekoweb.org) with pinned SHA-256 checksums, and installs it into /opt/septabee with standard operations. The deepseek model successfully reviewed this file and confirmed it is a standard desktop entry with no security issues.
data.disagreement_analysis: The disagreement was caused by a tool error (LLM API HTTP 400 BadRequestError) in the qwen model when attempting to review septabee.desktop, resulting in an inconclusive overall verdict. The deepseek model successfully reviewed all three files and found them safe. This is not a genuine security disagreement but a tooling failure.
coverage_issues: qwen model failed to review septabee.desktop due to API error (HTTP 400 BadRequestError)
learnings: Tool errors (API failures) should trigger automatic retries rather than immediately marking a file as inconclusive
When multiple models audit the same package, a tool error in one model should not override successful reviews from other models for the same file
The verdict aggregation logic should distinguish between 'inconclusive due to tool error' and 'inconclusive due to genuine security uncertainty' to avoid false escalation
